subject: ARA
label: Grade 05
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 05 Arabic, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Reading and comprehension
modules.outcome: answer questions on a longer text
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Reading and comprehension', you learn to answer questions on a longer text. Lessons are short and playful, with objects, pictures and talk. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Reading and comprehension' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: answer questions on a longer text, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: الولد يلعب في الحديقة. أين يلعب الولد؟ في الحديقة. (The boy plays in the garden. Where does the boy play? In the garden.) Method: Model run for 'Reading and comprehension'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Answer questions on a longer text: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Read the passage. ذَهَبَتِ الطَّالِبَةُ مَعَ صَدِيقَتِهَا إِلَى مَكْتَبَةِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ يَوْمَ الْخَمِيسِ. اسْتَعَارَتِ الطَّالِبَةُ كِتَابًا عَنِ الْحَيَوَانَاتِ، وَاخْتَارَتْ صَدِيقَتُهَا قِصَّةً عَنِ الْبَحْرِ. [The student went with her friend to the school library on Thursday. The student borrowed a book about animals, and her friend chose a story about the sea.]

Step 2, Read the rest. جَلَسَتَا مَعًا وَقَرَأَتَا بِهُدُوءٍ. فِي الْمَسَاءِ أَخْبَرَتِ الطَّالِبَةُ أُمَّهَا بِمَا تَعَلَّمَتْ. [The two sat together and read quietly. In the evening the student told her mother what she had learned.] Underline the day, the place and the people.

Step 3, Answer direct questions. مَتَى ذَهَبَتِ الطَّالِبَةُ إِلَى الْمَكْتَبَةِ؟ [When did the student go to the library?] ذَهَبَتْ يَوْمَ الْخَمِيسِ. [She went on Thursday.] مَاذَا اسْتَعَارَتْ؟ [What did she borrow?] اسْتَعَارَتْ كِتَابًا عَنِ الْحَيَوَانَاتِ. [She borrowed a book about animals.]

Step 4, Answer a thinking question. لِمَاذَا قَرَأَتَا بِهُدُوءٍ؟ [Why did they read quietly?] لِأَنَّهُمَا فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ. [Because they were in the library.] This reason is not written word for word, so use the clue كَانَتَا فِي مَكْتَبَةِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ [They were in the school library].

Step 5, Fix an error. A student writes the whole passage as an answer to مَنْ اخْتَارَ قِصَّةً؟ [Who chose a story?]. Correction: choose the key sentence only, اخْتَارَتْ صَدِيقَةُ الطَّالِبَةِ قِصَّةً. [The student's friend chose a story.] Short, exact answers score better.

Step 6, Your turn: give a title and answer: what did the student do in the evening? Model answer: عُنْوَانٌ: زِيَارَةُ الْمَكْتَبَةِ [Title: A visit to the library]. أَخْبَرَتِ الطَّالِبَةُ أُمَّهَا بِمَا تَعَلَّمَتْ. [The student told her mother what she learned.]

modules.title: Nominal and verbal sentences
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Nominal and verbal sentences', you learn to identify and write both types. Lessons are short and playful, with objects, pictures and talk. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Nominal and verbal sentences' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: identify and write both types, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: Nominal sentence starts with a noun: al-waladu mujtahidun (the boy is hardworking). Verbal sentence starts with a verb: dhahaba al-waladu ila al-madrasa (the boy went to school). Method: Model run for 'Nominal and verbal sentences'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Identify and write both types: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Meet the two types. A nominal sentence begins with a noun: الْوَلَدُ مُجْتَهِدٌ [The boy is hard-working]. It has a subject الْوَلَدُ and a predicate مُجْتَهِدٌ. A verbal sentence begins with a verb: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ [The boy wrote the lesson]. Always look at the first word.

Step 2, Sort by first word. السَّمَاءُ صَافِيَةٌ [The sky is clear] starts with a noun, so it is nominal. يَلْعَبُ الْأَطْفَالُ [The children play] starts with a verb, so it is verbal. أَكَلَتِ الْبِنْتُ التُّفَّاحَةَ [The girl ate the apple] starts with a verb, so it is verbal too.

Step 3, Name the parts of a verbal sentence. In كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ, the verb is كَتَبَ [wrote], the doer is الْوَلَدُ [the boy], ending in damma (ُ), and the object is الدَّرْسَ [the lesson], ending in fatha (َ). Order: verb, doer, object. Say it aloud, then point to each part.

Step 4, Match gender. In a nominal sentence the predicate agrees with the subject: الْوَلَدُ مُجْتَهِدٌ (boy, masculine) and الْبِنْتُ مُجْتَهِدَةٌ (girl, feminine). In a verbal sentence the verb agrees in gender too: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ, كَتَبَتِ الْبِنْتُ [The girl wrote]. When the verb comes first it stays singular: يَلْعَبُ الْأَوْلَادُ [The boys play].

Step 5, Watch the trap. الطَّالِبُ يَقْرَأُ [The student reads] begins with a noun, so it is a nominal sentence even though it contains a verb. Move the verb first and it becomes verbal: يَقْرَأُ الطَّالِبُ الْكِتَابَ [The student reads the book]. The type depends only on the first word.

Step 6, Your turn: label each sentence, then write one of your own. 1) الْبَابُ مَفْتُوحٌ [The door is open] 2) فَتَحَ الْوَلَدُ الْبَابَ [The boy opened the door]. Answer: 1 is nominal, it starts with the noun الْبَابُ; 2 is verbal, it starts with the verb فَتَحَ. Own sentence, for example: الْقَمَرُ جَمِيلٌ [The moon is beautiful], nominal.

modules.title: Sports and health
modules.outcome: talk about sport and healthy living
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Sports and health', you learn to talk about sport and healthy living. Lessons are short and playful, with objects, pictures and talk. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Sports and health' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: talk about sport and healthy living, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: أمارس الرياضة كل يوم وأشرب الماء. الرياضة مفيدة للصحة. (I exercise daily and drink water. Sport is good for health.) Method: Model run for 'Sports and health'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Talk about sport and healthy living: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Name sports. كُرَةُ الْقَدَمِ [football], كُرَةُ السَّلَّةِ [basketball], السِّبَاحَةُ [swimming], الْجَرْيُ [running], رُكُوبُ الدَّرَّاجَةِ [cycling]. Ask a partner: مَا رِيَاضَتُكَ الْمُفَضَّلَةُ؟ [What is your favourite sport?]

Step 2, Say what you do. أُمَارِسُ الرِّيَاضَةَ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ فِي الْأُسْبُوعِ. [I do sport three times a week.] أُحِبُّ السِّبَاحَةَ. [I like swimming.] أَجْرِي فِي الْحَدِيقَةِ كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ. [I run in the park every morning.]

Step 3, Talk about healthy living. أَشْرَبُ الْمَاءَ كَثِيرًا. [I drink a lot of water.] الْفَوَاكِهُ وَالْخُضَارُ مُفِيدَةٌ لِلْجِسْمِ. [Fruit and vegetables are good for the body.] كَثْرَةُ الْحَلْوَى مُضِرَّةٌ. [Too many sweets are harmful.] Say each sentence slowly.

Step 4, Give advice with يَجِبُ أَنْ. يَجِبُ أَنْ أَنَامَ مُبَكِّرًا. [I must sleep early.] يَجِبُ أَنْ نَأْكُلَ طَعَامًا صِحِّيًّا. [We must eat healthy food.] After أَنْ the present verb ends with a fatha sound: أَنَامَ، نَأْكُلَ.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says يَجِبُ أَنْ أَنَامُ مُبَكِّرًا. Correction: يَجِبُ أَنْ أَنَامَ مُبَكِّرًا, because the verb after أَنْ takes fatha. Another says أُحِبُّ السِّبَاحَةُ; use أُحِبُّ السِّبَاحَةَ.

Step 6, Your turn: write three sentences about your sport and a healthy habit. Model answer: أَلْعَبُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ. أَشْرَبُ الْمَاءَ كَثِيرًا. يَجِبُ أَنْ أَنَامَ مُبَكِّرًا. [I play football on Saturday. I drink a lot of water. I must sleep early.]

modules.title: Writing a paragraph
modules.outcome: write a paragraph with a topic
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Writing a paragraph', you learn to write a paragraph with a topic. Lessons are short and playful, with objects, pictures and talk. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Writing a paragraph' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: write a paragraph with a topic, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: فقرة: القراءة مفيدة. فهي تزيد معلوماتنا. وتنمّي لغتنا. لذلك أقرأ كل يوم. (topic sentence, two details, closing) Method: Model run for 'Writing a paragraph'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Write a paragraph with a topic: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, A paragraph has a topic sentence, two or three details, and a closing sentence. Choose a topic: my school. First write the topic sentence: مَدْرَسَتِي مَكَانٌ جَمِيلٌ لِلتَّعَلُّمِ. [My school is a lovely place to learn.]

Step 2, Add details that support the topic. فِيهَا صُفُوفٌ وَاسِعَةٌ وَمَلْعَبٌ كَبِيرٌ. [It has spacious classrooms and a big playground.] أُحِبُّ الْمُعَلِّمِينَ لِأَنَّهُمْ يَشْرَحُونَ بِصَبْرٍ. [I like the teachers because they explain patiently.]

Step 3, Use linking words. وَ [and], لِأَنَّ [because], ثُمَّ [then], لِذَلِكَ [therefore]. Example: أَدْرُسُ بِجِدٍّ لِأَنِّي أُحِبُّ الْعِلْمَ. [I study hard because I love knowledge.] Add one linking word to each detail.

Step 4, Close the paragraph. لِذَلِكَ أَنَا سَعِيدٌ فِي مَدْرَسَتِي. [Therefore I am happy in my school.] Now read the paragraph from the topic sentence to the end and check that every sentence talks about school.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student writes a paragraph about school and then adds أَنَا أُحِبُّ الْبَحْرَ [I love the sea], which is off topic. Correction: delete it, or replace it with a school detail like فِي مَدْرَسَتِي مَكْتَبَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ [My school has a big library].

Step 6, Your turn: write a four-sentence paragraph on my family. Model answer: أُسْرَتِي صَغِيرَةٌ وَسَعِيدَةٌ. فِيهَا أَبِي وَأُمِّي وَأَخِي. نَأْكُلُ مَعًا كُلَّ مَسَاءٍ. لِذَلِكَ أُحِبُّ أُسْرَتِي. [My family is small and happy. It has my father, mother and brother. We eat together every evening. Therefore I love my family.]

ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
